newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH RAPESEED WORSE, WHEAT/RYE BETTER THAN IN 96.
newsitem.headline: POLISH RAPESEED WORSE, WHEAT/RYE BETTER THAN IN 96.

text.p: Polish winter rapeseed crops suffered more damage this winter than last year, but winter wheat and rye crops are in better shape, preliminary figures from the Agriculture Ministry showed on Tuesday.

Bozena Nowicka, deputy head of the Ministry's Production Department, told Reuters that 46 percent of rapeseed crops did not survive the winter, while eight percent of wheat and two percent of rye froze over the cold 1996/97 winter.
Last year 61 percent of rapeseed survived the winter, while 89 percent of wheat and 90 of rye successfully sprouted in 1996, according to Central Statistical Office (GUS) data.
"According to our preliminary figures winter losses are huge...and final results may even be worse," Nowicka said.
Nowicka said that low night-time temperatures and warm days often froze and refroze topsoil destroyig crops.
She also said 41 percent of winter barley crops has been destroyed by the winter against 19 percent losses last year.
"Although winter barley was sown on only about 100,000 hectars losses are large and farmers are looking to replow fields with either spring barley or wheat," Nowicka said.
She said demand for spring grain and rapeseed seed was rising and said that winter losses could be minimized by favourable weather in the spring and summer.
GUS is due to release official damage figures for the 1996/97 winter early next month.
